items.headline: Man, 27, charged with insulting Islam after being deported from Malaysia
items.summary: The man, deported from Malaysia on 6 August over social-media videos making profane remarks about the Muslim community, was arrested on arrival in Singapore and charged on 7 August under the Maintenance of Religious Harmony Act.

items.headline: Boy, 13, needs seven stitches after an alleged assault by a classmate
items.summary: A 13-year-old Singaporean boy was allegedly spat on and thrown against a pillar by a classmate, leaving him with seven stitches to his upper lip; the family has lodged a police report.

items.headline: Singapore marks its 61st National Day this weekend under a 'Go Beyond' theme
items.summary: The Republic celebrates its 61st birthday on 9 August; PM Lawrence Wong is due to deliver his National Day Message before the parade, with the National Day Rally set for 23 August.

items.headline: Man, 68, jailed 11 years and six months for abusing his step-granddaughter
items.summary: A 68-year-old Singaporean man was sentenced to 11 years and six months' jail for the repeated sexual abuse of his step-granddaughter, who was 11 at the time.

items.headline: Parliament clears a bill raising the Supreme Court's sanctioned strength to 38 judges
items.summary: The Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Bill, 2026 lifts the sanctioned strength from 34 to 38 including the Chief Justice, the first increase since 2019.

items.headline: Delhi court extends custody of 13 NEET-UG paper-leak accused as CBI files chargesheet
items.summary: The Rouse Avenue court extended the judicial custody of all 13 accused in the NEET-UG 2026 paper-leak case to 10 August, with the CBI's chargesheet taken up on 7 August.

items.headline: Centre tells the Supreme Court a 'creamy layer' for SC/STs is Parliament's call
items.summary: In a counter-affidavit, the Union government said applying the creamy-layer principle to Scheduled Castes and Tribes is a legislative question for Parliament, not the judiciary.

items.headline: India adds heatwaves and lightning to its notified natural-disaster list
items.summary: The Home Ministry told the Lok Sabha that heatwaves and lightning are now notified calamities eligible for SDRF and NDRF relief, on the 16th Finance Commission's advice, taking the total to 14.

items.headline: UK house prices flat in July as the market cools for the summer
items.summary: The Lloyds/Halifax index showed the average UK home edged down to £299,253 in July, with annual growth easing to 1.3% and agreed sales down about 9% year on year.

items.headline: Chancellor John Healey sets the autumn Budget for 28 October
items.summary: Chancellor John Healey confirmed the Burnham government's first Budget will be delivered on 28 October, keeping to a single major fiscal event a year.

items.headline: Burnham declines to rule out tax rises to fund social care
items.summary: PM Andy Burnham did not rule out tax increases to pay for social-care changes, as analysts said his devolution push could hand London greater powers over taxation.

items.headline: UK retail sales keep falling but at a slower pace, CBI survey shows
items.summary: The CBI's distributive-trades survey showed retail sales volumes fell at a weighted balance of -26% in the year to July, up from -54% in June, as rail strikes added pressure.

items.headline: At least seven killed as a 14-year-old opens fire at a school near Bangkok
items.summary: A 14-year-old student killed his grandparents then opened fire at Debsirin School in Nonthaburi on 7 August, killing at least seven people before taking his own life; PM Anutin Charnvirakul called it premeditated.

items.headline: A fresh wave of US tariffs on about 60 economies takes effect
items.summary: New US import tariffs of roughly 10% to 12.5% on dozens of trading partners took effect on 7 August, replacing steeper duties struck down earlier this year by the Supreme Court.

items.headline: US Senate opens debate on a Russia sanctions bill as Ukraine strikes refineries
items.summary: The US Senate began floor debate on a long-stalled Russia sanctions bill on 7 August, as Zelensky said Ukrainian strikes hit Russian oil refineries and Black Sea vessels; a Russian strike damaged a stadium in Odesa.

items.headline: UN warns of atrocity risk in the besieged Sudanese city of el-Obeid
items.summary: UN officials warned that el-Obeid, encircled by the RSF, risks becoming the next el-Fasher as residents endure drone strikes, water shortages and cholera; the RSF intensified attacks after the army secured a key highway.

items.headline: Apple struggles to keep MacBook Air in stock amid a memory squeeze
items.summary: Bloomberg reported that some MacBook Air configurations face delivery waits of about a month, as a tightening memory-chip market driven by AI demand squeezes consumer supply.

items.headline: EU rules requiring AI systems to identify themselves take effect
items.summary: Under Article 50 of the EU AI Act, in force from 2 August, providers must disclose when people interact with chatbots and clearly label AI-generated deepfakes.

items.headline: Fireworks AI raises about $1.5 billion to help firms specialise AI models
items.summary: Inference startup Fireworks AI closed a Series D of roughly $1.5 billion for tools that turn general-purpose models into specialised systems trained on customers' own data.

items.headline: The Friend AI pendant relaunches with a new voice and a higher price
items.summary: The Verge reported that the Friend wearable, an always-listening AI companion pendant, returned with a redesigned voice and a raised price.

items.headline: US payrolls unexpectedly fall 23,000 in July as hiring stalls
items.summary: Nonfarm payrolls dropped by 23,000 in July against expectations of a gain of around 80,000, with 53,000 lost government jobs; unemployment edged down to 4.1% and wage growth cooled to 3.2%.

items.headline: Wall Street rallies to records as a weak jobs report lifts rate-cut hopes
items.summary: The S&P 500 rose 0.62% to a record 7,757.64 on 7 August, the Dow added 151.83 points to 54,036.93 and the Nasdaq climbed 1.3% to 26,690.62, its strongest week since April.

items.headline: The Trade Desk sinks about 22% on a rare revenue miss
items.summary: The Trade Desk fell roughly 22% after Q2 revenue rose just 3% to $715.1 million, missing estimates, while its Q3 guidance of about $650 million came in well below forecasts.

items.headline: Take-Two rises about 6% after its quarterly results
items.summary: Take-Two Interactive shares gained about 6% after the Grand Theft Auto publisher reported fiscal first-quarter results.

items.headline: 🎾 Fernandez ousts Andreeva as Sabalenka and Rybakina reach the Toronto last 16
items.summary: Leylah Fernandez beat Mirra Andreeva 6-2, 6-2 in the third round at the WTA 1000 in Toronto to reach the last 16, where Aryna Sabalenka and Elena Rybakina also advanced.

items.headline: 🎾 Fils and Lehecka reach the Montreal last 16 as seeds keep tumbling
items.summary: Arthur Fils and Jiri Lehecka won their third-round matches at the ATP Masters 1000 in Montreal to reach the last 16, after top seed Zverev and fourth seed Medvedev had already fallen.

items.headline: 🏏 Sunrisers Leeds women thrash Birmingham Phoenix by nine wickets
items.summary: Chasing 108, Sunrisers Leeds won by nine wickets in The Hundred with 31 balls to spare, Phoebe Litchfield unbeaten on 71 to take player of the match.

items.headline: 🏎️ Verstappen picks out Antonelli as the standout of F1's first half
items.summary: With the season in its summer shutdown, Max Verstappen praised championship leader Kimi Antonelli, who takes a lead of about 50 points over Lewis Hamilton into the break before the Dutch GP on 21-23 August.

items.headline: Physicists steer heat like a beam of light through a crystal at room temperature
items.summary: UCLA engineers reported in Nature Physics that they guided phonons along ray-like paths in boron arsenide at room temperature, an effect previously seen only near absolute zero.

items.headline: The brain's memory centre swaps out its immune cells around age 50
items.summary: A long-term study found the hippocampus loses many long-resident immune cells from around age 50 and replaces them with more inflammatory ones, a possible clue to Alzheimer's.

items.headline: Flatworm immune cells self-destruct to kill invaders, then vanish
items.summary: Stanford researchers described immune cells in flatworms that swarm invaders, explode within minutes to destroy them, then disappear completely.

items.headline: NASA readies its Roman telescope, a machine built to find 100,000 planets
items.summary: NASA is preparing the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope for a launch later this month; the observatory is projected to discover more than 100,000 planets.

fun_fact.headline: A day on Venus is longer than a year on Venus
fun_fact.body: A day on Venus lasts longer than a year on Venus. The planet turns on its axis just once every 243 Earth days, but it circles the Sun in about 225 Earth days — so a single Venusian rotation outlasts a full Venusian orbit. Stranger still, Venus spins backwards, so the Sun there rises in the west and sets in the east.

puzzle.title: Boxes Within Boxes
puzzle.body: In a grid 4 squares wide and 4 squares tall, how many rectangles of any size can you find (single cells, the whole 4x4 square, and everything in between)?
puzzle.approach: A rectangle is any box you can trace, of any size — not just the little cells.
puzzle.answer: 100 rectangles. Choose 2 of the 5 vertical lines and 2 of the 5 horizontal lines: C(5,2) x C(5,2) = 10 x 10 = 100. (30 of them are perfect squares.)

word_puzzle.title: Count Me In
word_puzzle.body: Letter Boxed. TOP: M,C,U / RIGHT: I,O,T / BOTTOM: S,N,L / LEFT: A,G,E. Use all 12 letters; consecutive letters from different sides; each new word starts with the previous word's last letter.
word_puzzle.approach: Chain two words covering all 12 letters, jumping sides on every step.
word_puzzle.answer: MISCOUNT -> TANGLE (covers all 12 letters; every consecutive pair is on a different side).
